title: Reversible Billing Status Replay
prompt:
Rebuild per-account balances from an unordered transaction log. Implement `BillingStatus(monetary_columns)` and `replay_billing_transactions(monetary_columns, transactions)`. The latter returns `{user_id: amounts_dict}`.

`transactions` maps a unique transaction ID to a row with `user_id` and integer `timestamp`. Replay rows in ascending `(timestamp, transaction_id)` order. Every status starts every configured monetary column at `0`; a missing monetary column in a row leaves it unchanged.

A normal row adds each supplied monetary value. A row with `overwrite=True` instead replaces only its supplied columns. A row with `undo_last=True` reverts that user's most recent effective normal row; `redo_last=True` reapplies that user's most recently undone row. Command rows ignore all monetary fields and never enter history. An undo or redo with no applicable history is a no-op. A new normal row clears that user's redo history, even when it changes no monetary column; empty normal rows themselves are not undoable.

Undo and redo must work for both additive and overwrite rows. A user appearing only in a command or empty row must still appear in the returned mapping with all-zero balances. Treat control flags as mutually exclusive and use only the Python standard library.

example.reasoning: The replay order is timestamp-first, but the two independent monetary updates both remain in the final account state.
